title: ARIA Roles: Building Semantic Widgets 🧱
description: Explore widget, landmark, and document structure roles that extend HTML semantics.

slides.title: The Role Attribute 🎭
slides.content:
`role="..."` tells assistive technology what an element represents.

* **Landmark roles** – `banner`, `navigation`, `main`, `complementary`, `contentinfo` (usually not needed because HTML5 elements map to these).
* **Widget roles** – `tab`, `tabpanel`, `slider`, `menu`, `toolbar`.
* **Document structure** – `list`, `listitem`, `group`, `region`.

Adding a role does **not** add keyboard support. That's on you.

quizData.question: What role would you assign to a container of tab buttons?
quizData.explanation: The group of tabs gets `role="tablist"`, each tab gets `role="tab"`, and the content panes get `role="tabpanel"`.

slides.title: Important: Role ≠ Keyboard Behaviour ⌨️
slides.content:
Using `role="button"` does not make a `<div>` respond to Enter or Space. You must add:

* `tabindex="0"` to make it focusable.
* JavaScript event listeners for `keydown` (Space, Enter).

Semantic HTML elements give you all that for free. ARIA is a promise you must keep.

quizData.question: What must you add to a `<div role="button">` to make it focusable?
quizData.explanation: `tabindex="0"` puts the element in the natural tab order.

slides.title: Common ARIA Roles Cheat Sheet 📋
slides.content:
* `alert` – important, time‑sensitive notification.
* `alertdialog` – modal alert with interactive controls.
* `dialog` – a window over the main content.
* `tooltip` – a popup that displays info.
* `switch` – a toggle (like a checkbox but immediate).

Always refer to the [ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) for expected behaviour.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Don't Duplicate Semantics
If an element already has a native role (`<button>` → button), do not add `role="button"`. Redundant roles can confuse assistive tech.
